recent_open_items.title: status: compare against both upstream and push branch by default
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Make `@{upstream} @{push}` the default for `status.compareBranches`. With the default `push.default` of `simple` the output does not change. With `current` or `matching`, a branch pushed somewhere other than its upstream now shows both comparisons.

Changes in v2:
- Kept the existing tests unchanged, including the explicit `"@{upstream} @{push}"` config and the `"@{upstream}"` test on `main`
- Added tests for the new default with the same upstream and push branch, in a triangular workflow, and without an upstream
- Added a test showing that `"@{upstream}"` restores the old output on a triangular branch
- Reworded the commit message to point to 3ea95ac9c5 and explain which setups see a change

cc: Phillip Wood <phillip.wood123@gmail.com>
cc: "Kristoffer Haugsbakk" <kristofferhaugsbakk@fastmail.com>

recent_open_items.title: config: make the suggested "set" command safe to paste
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
When `git config <key>=<value>` is given a value with spaces, the suggested command fails when pasted back into a shell. Quote the value when it needs it and put the command on its own line, the way other hints show commands:

```
$ git config status.comparebranches="@{upstream} @{push}"
error: missing value to set to the variable 'status.comparebranches=@{upstream} @{push}'
hint: did you mean:
hint:
hint: 	git config set status.comparebranches '@{upstream} @{push}'
```

recent_open_items.title: store: share concurrent reads of the same commit or tree
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
As we improve concurrency (e.g. the recent changes that made `MergedTree::entries()` concurrent), we increase the risk of concurrent requests to the backend if the object is not in `Store`'s caches. Another example is `jj log --no-graph -p`, which diffs each commit against its parent, so the parent's tree is read both for the parent's diff and for its child's diff. I'm about to make `jj log -p` (i.e. with the graph) also read commits concurrently.

This patch makes concurrent cache misses for the same commit or tree share a single backend read. Every caller waiting for the read polls it, so it makes progress even if the caller that started it is not being polled. That happens e.g. when a commit is prefetched by a buffered stream and the consumer of the stream reads the same commit as the parent of an earlier commit in the stream.

recent_open_items.title: Avoid holding mwindow mutex during pack and window allocations
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
**Summary**:  libgit2 can deadlock when holding git_mwindow__mutex across allocations if a custom allocator, under GC pressure, runs a finalizer that re-enters libgit2 and tries to acquire the same mutex.

---

When libgit2 is configured with a custom allocator via GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR (such as in Ruby/Rugged bindings), memory allocations can trigger a garbage collection cycle. If the GC finalizer frees an unreachable repository, git_repository_free calls git_mwindow_put_pack, which attempts to acquire git_mwindow__mutex.

Previously, git_mwindow_get_pack held git_mwindow__mutex across git_packfile_alloc. When an allocation triggered a GC pass, the thread deadlocked on the non-recursive mutex with itself. A similar issue existed in git_mwindow_open when allocating git_mwindow structures.

recent_open_items.title: remote: honor negative refspecs after fetching
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Fixes #7435.

Negative fetch refspecs already affect negotiation, but positive matches can select excluded refs again after downloading. This can update excluded remote-tracking refs, include them in FETCH_HEAD, and prune them when their source disappears.

This change applies exclusions when updating tips and when matching active or configured refspecs for opportunistic updates. Pruning checks exclusions against each reverse-mapped source. Negative refspecs do not independently select refs; tag auto-following remains unchanged.

Eight tests cover reference creation, preservation of existing refs, FETCH_HEAD, wildcard exclusions, pruning, active and configured exclusions during opportunistic updates, and tag auto-following. Seven regression tests fail on the original code; the tag auto-follow control passes.

Validation on Fedora AArch64:
- Debug build with USE_SSH=exec.
- 23 fetchlocal tests pass.
- Related network, remote, FETCH_HEAD, and non-network clone tests pass (204 tests).

recent_open_items.title: remote: honor explicit tag fetch destinations
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
In AUTO tag mode, `refs/tags/hard_tag:refs/custom/tag` silently ignores the requested destination, and `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` does not replace an existing tag. Tag auto-following currently runs before the explicit refspec mapping.

Prefer a matching refspec with a destination before applying auto-following. This honors the destination and force flag and keeps the output buffer empty for exact refspec transforms.

Three regression tests fail before the fix and pass afterward: exact destination, wildcard destination, and forced update. A fourth checks that ordinary auto-following preserves an existing local tag.

Validation on Fedora AArch64: all 201 selected remote, local-fetch, fetch, and FETCH_HEAD tests pass.

Fixes #7438.
